# peq

[![GitHub Actions](https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/actions/workflows/ci.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/actions)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

A CLI tool that analyzes PHP code dependencies and visualizes the blast radius of changes.

`peq <symbol>` draws what one symbol reaches. `peq graph '<query>'` answers a question about the whole dependency graph, written in [GQL](https://www.iso.org/standard/76120.html).

## Requirements

- PHP 8.1 or higher

## Installation

Download the PHAR from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/releases):

```bash
curl -Lo peq.phar https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/releases/latest/download/peq.phar
chmod +x peq.phar
sudo mv peq.phar /usr/local/bin/peq
```

Or install via Composer:

```bash
composer require --dev k-kinzal/peq
```

## Usage

```console
$ peq 'App\Domain\Invoice' src
App\Domain\Invoice
├── App\Domain\Invoice::total
│   └── App\Domain\Money::add
└── App\Domain\Invoice::lines
    └── App\Domain\Money::add (*)
```

```
Usage:
  peq [options] [--] <target> [<path>]

Arguments:
  target                     Namespace\ClassName, Namespace\ClassName::methodName or Namespace\functionName
  path                       Base directory to analyze (default: current working dir)

Options:
      --config=CONFIG        Path to config file (default: <cwd>/.peq.yaml)
  -D, --direction=DIRECTION  Dependency direction: uses|used-by (default: uses)
  -R, --reverse              Shortcut for --direction used-by
  -L, --level=LEVEL          Limit depth of the dependency graph
  -O, --output=OUTPUT        Output format (tree|json|dot|table|graph|mermaid)
  -I, --include=INCLUDE      Include patterns (multiple values allowed)
  -E, --exclude=EXCLUDE      Exclude patterns (multiple values allowed)
      --type=TYPE            Analyzer type (phpstan|native|debug)
      --memory-limit=MEMORY-LIMIT  Memory limit (e.g. 1G, 256M)
```

`--direction used-by` (or `-R`) walks the other way: what depends on the symbol, which is what a change to it can break.

## Output formats

| `--output` | What it writes |
|------------|----------------|
| `tree`     | An indented tree, the way `tree` draws a directory. The default. `(*)` marks a symbol expanded elsewhere, `(recursive)` a cycle. |
| `json`     | One entry per symbol: kind, depth, parent, the relations that led to it, and where it is declared. |
| `table`    | One row per symbol: depth, symbol, kind and `file:line`. |
| `graph`    | The graph itself, drawn in the terminal: every symbol once, joined by arrows, as wide as the terminal and as long as it needs to be. |
| `mermaid`  | The same graph as a Mermaid flowchart, for a pull request or a design note. |
| `dot`      | The same graph as a Graphviz digraph. |

```console
$ peq 'App\Domain\Invoice' src --output=graph
                     ┌──▶ App\Domain\Invoice::total ──┐
App\Domain\Invoice ──┤                                ├──▶ App\Domain\Money::add
                     └──▶ App\Domain\Invoice::lines ──┘
```

```console
$ peq 'App\Domain\Invoice' src --output=mermaid
flowchart LR
    n1["App\Domain\Invoice"]
    n2["App\Domain\Invoice::total"]
    n3["App\Domain\Invoice::lines"]
    n4["App\Domain\Money::add"]
    n1 -->|"declaration-method"| n2
    n1 -->|"declaration-method"| n3
    n2 -->|"method-call"| n4
    n3 -->|"method-call"| n4
```

```bash
peq 'App\Domain\Invoice' src --output=dot | dot -Tsvg -o invoice.svg
```

## Querying the graph

`peq graph` takes a query in GQL, the ISO standard query language for graphs, and answers with a table:

```console
$ peq graph 'MATCH (c:Class)-[:declaresMethod]->(m:Method WHERE m.visibility = '"'"'public'"'"')
             RETURN c.name AS class, count(m) AS methods
             GROUP BY class ORDER BY methods DESC LIMIT 3' src
+----------------+-----------------+
| class (STRING) | methods (INT64) |
+----------------+-----------------+
| TokenReader    | 17              |
| RawConfig      | 12              |
| Graph          | 9               |
+----------------+-----------------+
```

`peq graph --schema` lists the labels, properties and functions a query can use, each written the way a query has to write it. A few of peq's names spell words GQL reserves — `` `call` ``, `` `Function` ``, `` `value` `` — and are written in back quotes, so quote a query with `'` rather than `"`.

`--output` takes the same formats as above: `graph`, `mermaid` and `dot` draw the part of the graph the answer holds, and `tree` draws the paths it bound. `--hops` sets the largest upper bound a repetition such as `{1,6}` may be written with (10 by default).

## Analyzers

| `--type`  | What it does | Where it is available |
|-----------|--------------|-----------------------|
| `phpstan` | Builds the graph from PHPStan's analysis. The reference engine. | Installed from source or via Composer |
| `native`  | Reads the sources directly with a parser. Between 13x and 59x faster, and checked to build the same graph. | Everywhere, including the released PHAR |

The released PHAR carries only `native`.

## Configuration

Create a `.peq.yaml` file in your project root to set default options:

```yaml
type: native
output: tree
hops: 10
excludes:
  - vendor
  - vendor-bin
  - .git
  - tests
```

Configuration is resolved by merging 4 layers (later layers override earlier ones):

1. Default values
2. Environment variables (`PEQ_*`)
3. YAML config file (`.peq.yaml`)
4. CLI options

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the LICENSE file for details.

# Agents

A CLI tool that analyzes PHP code dependencies and visualizes the blast radius of changes. `peq <symbol>` draws what one symbol reaches, as a tree, for a person; `peq graph '<query>'` answers whatever can be written in GQL, as a table, for a program or an agent. Both write the same set of formats.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP**: 8.1 / 8.2 / 8.3 / 8.4 / 8.5

## Core Concepts

- **Impact analysis is the primary goal** — automatically identify what breaks when a class, method, or function changes
- **Bidirectional traversal** — walk the graph in two directions: `uses` (what the target depends on) and `used-by` (what depends on the target)
- **Reporter switching** — `--output` picks how one walk is written down: `tree` for a person, `json` for a program or an agent, `dot` for a renderer, `table` for a review, `graph` for the wiring rather than the shape. Where the walk stops is decided once, by `Expansion`, so no format can disagree with another about what is affected
- **GQL is the query language** — `peq graph` runs ISO/IEC 39075 GQL, the standard the SQL committee publishes, so an agent already knows it; an invented syntax would have to be explained in every prompt. It runs that and nothing more: a word the standard does not define is a word peq refuses, which `composer spec` checks against ISO's own grammar artifact. Read-only by design: nothing in the language can change a graph peq has just read out of source code
- **Two engines, one graph** — `PhpStanAnalyzer` is the reference; `NativeAnalyzer` reads sources directly and is checked against it by comparing canonical graph snapshots. A change to either must keep them identical
- **The binary carries one engine** — `phpstan/phpstan` is a dev dependency, so the PHAR holds only `NativeAnalyzer`. `AnalyzerKind` offers a kind only when what it is built on is installed
- **Graph model** — bidirectional adjacency list of nodes (Class, Method, Function, etc. — 11 kinds) and edges (MethodCall, Extends, etc. — 22 kinds). Inverse edges (UsedBy, DeclaredIn) are generated automatically when an edge is added

## Project Tradeoff Sliders

│   ├── Argument/    # Reading a value as the kind an operation needs
│   ├── Binding/     # The rows a clause is given and produces
│   ├── Element/     # The analysed graph as labelled elements a query can match
│   ├── Evaluation/  # Operators, under three-valued logic
│   ├── Invocation/  # The built-in functions and the aggregates
│   ├── Matching/    # Finding every way a pattern matches
│   ├── Execution/   # Running the clauses, and combining query blocks
│   └── Result/      # The answer: columns, rows and a GQLSTATUS
└── Reporter/        # Output formatters and traversal strategies
    ├── Traversal/   # How the graph is walked
    ├── Diagram/     # Drawing a graph in a terminal, shared by both commands
    ├── TreeReporter/     # An indented tree, for a person
    ├── JsonReporter/     # A JSON document, for a program
    ├── DotReporter/      # A Graphviz digraph, for a renderer
    ├── TableReporter/    # A table of rows, for a review
    ├── GraphReporter/    # The graph itself, numbered, for the wiring
    └── Query/            # The same formats, for what a query answered
tests/               # Mirrors src/ namespaces. Keep fixtures next to the code they test
config/              # DI container wiring (services.php)
bin/                 # Entry point (console)
```

## Build & Test Commands

- `composer install` — install dependencies and `vendor-bin/` tools
- `composer test` — run PHPUnit (random order, `APP_ENV=test`). Append `-- tests/App/...` or `--filter testName` to narrow scope. The run needs room: two suites analyse peq's own sources with PHPStan in process, which costs most of a gigabyte each and grows with `src`, so `phpunit.xml.dist` allows 4G
- `composer test:equivalence` — read every installed dependency with both engines and fail on any difference
- `composer spec` — run the Behat specification of ISO/IEC 39075 against the query engine. Append `-- --tags='@feature:G011'` to run the scenarios that state one feature of the standard
- `composer lint` — run PHP CS Fixer + PHPStan (max level)
- `composer format` — apply PHP CS Fixer
- `composer compile` — build PHAR with Box after lint/tests pass
- `bin/console Namespace\\Class::method /path -L 3 --exclude vendor` — inspect dependencies. Use `--direction=used-by` for reverse traversal, and `--type=native` for the faster engine
- `bin/console Namespace\\Class::method /path --output=json` — write the same walk as JSON. `--output` takes `tree|json|dot|table|graph`
- ``bin/console graph 'MATCH (m:Method)-[:`call`]->(t) RETURN m.id, t.id' /path`` — query the graph in GQL. `--schema` writes the labels, properties and functions a query can use, each spelled the way a query has to write it. Quote a query with `'`: six of peq's own names spell words GQL reserves, so they are written in back quotes, which a double-quoted shell argument would take for command substitution

## Adding an Output Format

A format is one arm of one match. `OutputFormat` is a closed set, `ReporterFactory`
answers every case of it, and a case added without an arm is a static analysis error
rather than a runtime surprise.

What a new reporter must not do is decide where the walk stops. The level bound, the
cycle, the symbol expanded on another branch and the kind with nothing below it are
`Expansion`'s decisions, handed over as a `Continuation`; a reporter chooses what to
draw for each one. That is what makes `tests/Unit/Reporter/ReporterTest.php` — which
runs every reporter over the same graph — a contract rather than a smoke test, and it
is why the four formats can be compared line for line.

A reporter in a directory of its own needs a `deptrac.yaml` layer of its own. Without
one its boundaries are unenforced while the report still reads zero violations, which
is how the native analyzer shipped unchecked for a release.

## Keeping the Two Engines Identical
## Adding to the Query Language

The language is not ours to extend. A clause, an operator or a function that GQL does
not define does not belong in `src/Gql`, however useful it would be: the reason the
command is worth having is that a reader already knows what it accepts, and every
addition of our own makes that less true.

What is ours is the vocabulary a query is written against — the labels a symbol
carries, the properties it offers. Adding one means teaching `NodeLabels`,
`NodeProperties` or their edge counterparts, and adding it to `GraphSchema` so that
`--schema` still answers what a query may write. A name that spells a word GQL reserves
is allowed and costs its user back quotes; `GraphSchema` reports every name already
written that way, so the schema is always something a query can be pasted from.

That rule is enforced rather than trusted, in two places.

`composer spec` runs the conformance claim itself: a Behat specification under `spec/`,
written against ISO/IEC 39075 and its published digital artifacts, which are checked in
under `spec/iso/` with the checksums ISO publishes them under. Clause 24 makes a
conformance claim a register of the optional features implemented, so
`spec/features/conformance.feature` is that register — all 228 of them — and the suite
fails if the register names a feature the standard does not define, omits one it does,
claims a feature no scenario states, or states a feature the register does not claim.
Adding a feature to the claim therefore costs a scenario tagged with its code.

Seven further steps are what keep the language itself honest, each reading what is
published rather than what was remembered:

- the words `ReservedWords::WORDS` holds are `<reserved word>` and `<pre-reserved word>`
  of `spec/iso/gql.bnf.xml`, in the order the artifact writes them
- every upper-case word written as a literal anywhere in `src/Gql` is a `<kw>` of that
  same grammar, so an operator of our own fails before it is used
- every function and aggregate peq offers is a name that grammar writes a left
  parenthesis after, which a word merely appearing in it is not: `LABELS` is in there,
  in the syntax for declaring a graph type, and `labels(x)` is still not GQL
- every GQLSTATUS is one `spec/iso/conditions.xml` defines, worded as it words it
- everything peq settles for itself is an item `spec/iso/implementation-defined.xml`
  leaves to an implementation, named by its code
- every subclause a scenario is tagged with is one `spec/iso/subclauses.txt` numbers,
  because a number beside a familiar title is the easiest thing here to get wrong
- every artifact the six steps above read still has the SHA-256 sum it arrived under,
  which is what stops an artifact being edited until it agrees with `src/`

A new keyword, operator, function or status therefore fails the specification before it
reaches a reader. The specification is the one place the language's behaviour is stated;
PHPUnit tests under `tests/Unit` state what each class does, not what GQL is.

Add peq graph: query the dependency graph in GQL
feat/gql-graph
OPEN
## What this adds

A `graph` subcommand that takes a GQL query and runs it against the dependency graph.

```console
$ peq graph 'MATCH (m:Method)-[:`call`]->{1,3}(c:Method)
             WHERE right(m.owner, 10) = "Controller" AND right(c.owner, 5) = "Cache"
             RETURN m.id AS entry, c.id AS cache, m.file AS file, m.line AS line' src
```

The root command answers one question — what does this symbol reach — in the shape a
person reads. This one answers whatever question the reader can write, in the shape a
program reads. They are deliberately different tools: a reviewer wants a tree; an agent
working out whether a change is safe wants to ask "which public methods of a controller
reach the cache, and on which lines", get a table back, and act on it.

The language is [GQL](https://www.iso.org/standard/76120.html), the ISO standard the SQL
committee publishes, rather than something invented here. That is the whole reason for
the choice: a model that has read about graph databases has already read about GQL, so
the query language needs no explaining in the prompt that uses it.

## How the conformance claim is proved

ISO/IEC 39075 publishes no executable test suite for GQL and recognises none, so there
is no pass to point at. What its clause 24 asks for instead is a *claim*, and ISO
publishes the enumerations a claim is made of as machine-readable **digital artifacts**,
each with a header saying it exists for implementers to use. `composer spec` is that
claim, as **133 Behat scenarios** under `spec/`, checked against four of those artifacts
— which are checked in at `spec/iso/` under the checksums ISO publishes them with.

**The register.** `spec/features/conformance.feature` answers for all **228 optional
features** the standard defines — 37 claimed, 191 declined, none left silent — and five
steps make it a claim rather than an assertion: every code is looked up in
`features.xml`, every description is compared with the standard's wording, the register
must answer for every feature, every claimed feature must be stated by a tagged scenario
of this suite, and no scenario may state a feature the register does not claim. Claiming
a feature therefore costs a scenario.

**Seven more steps settle what a register cannot**, each reading something published:

| Step | Read from |
|------|-----------|
| every GQLSTATUS peq reports is one the standard defines, worded as it words it | `conditions.xml` |
| the words peq reserves are `<reserved word>` and `<pre-reserved word>`, in that order | `gql.bnf.xml` |
| every upper-case word written anywhere in `src/Gql` is a word the grammar writes | `gql.bnf.xml` |
| every function peq offers is a name the grammar writes a left parenthesis after | `gql.bnf.xml` |
| everything peq settles for itself is something the standard left it to settle | `implementation-defined.xml` |
| every subclause a scenario points at is one the standard numbers | `subclauses.txt` |
| every artifact the steps above read is the file it arrived as | `SHA256SUMS` |

The last one is what stops the rest being circular: an artifact edited until it agreed
with `src/` would otherwise let every other step pass.

**peq claims no extension under 24.5.3.** Writing the specification found eight defects,
all fixed here — three by the earlier contract suites, five by the steps above:

1. peq reported GQLSTATUS `42003`, which no part of ISO/IEC 39075 defines. It now
   reports `42000`.
2. It worded `42001` and `42002` more briefly than the standard words them.
3. It accepted `!=`. GQL spells inequality `<>` and nothing else.
4. A summary over a group list collapsed the table, where the standard says horizontal
   aggregation takes precedence over vertical aggregation.
5. **It reserved no word**, so `(:Function)` parsed where GQL asks for
   `` (:`Function`) ``, and `n.value` where it asks for ``n.`value` ``. All 262 reserved
   words — `<reserved word>` plus the `<pre-reserved word>`s held back for later
   editions — are now in `ReservedWords`, and `NameReader` applies them at the three
   positions the grammar distinguishes.
6. **It offered `CONTAINS`, `STARTS WITH` and `ENDS WITH`.** The Fabric documentation
   prints them and its own reserved word table marks all three as Fabric's extensions;
   ISO's grammar writes none of them. A prefix is now `left(s, n) = ...` and a suffix
   `right(s, n) = ...`, which is the standard's `<substring function>`.
7. **It offered `nodes`, `edges`, `labels`, `string_join` and `to_json_string`**, five
   functions the grammar never calls. `elements(p)` takes a path apart, a pattern asks
   about labels, and `--output=json` writes a row out.
8. **It answered a run of clauses that never said what to show.** A GQL linear query
   ends in a `RETURN` or a `FINISH`; `RETURN *` is how the language asks for everything
   bound.

The PHPUnit suites under `tests/Contract/Gql/` still check the same engine against the
[Fabric documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/graph/gql-language-guide),
which is a second reading of the same standard. Where the two disagree, ISO decides —
and where that documentation prints something Fabric added to GQL, the contract is now
that peq *refuses* it, so the disagreement is checked rather than described.

**Six of peq's own names spell words GQL reserves** — the labels `Function` and
`Unknown`, the family `call`, and the properties `value`, `abstract` and `parameters`.
They keep their names and cost a query its back quotes, because renaming peq's data to
suit the language would be the wrong way round. `--schema` reports every name already
written the way a query has to write it, so an agent copying from it never writes a
pattern that will not parse.

## Three pieces

**Nodes now record what a declaration says, not only that it exists.** A symbol used to
be a name, a kind and a place. It now also carries its visibility, its modifiers, its
attributes, its declared type, its assigned value and — for a callable — the signature
its callers were written against. Both analyzers record them through one shared reader,
so the native and PHPStan back ends agree about what a declaration says. The tree report
is unchanged; this is what the query language selects on.

**A GQL engine over the graph.** Lexer, parser, syntax tree, three-valued logic, pattern
matching, aggregation and result tables, under GQLSTATUS conditions. It covers every
statement, operator and function the documentation lists for reading a graph, plus the
set operators the guide lists as not yet supported in Fabric — `UNION DISTINCT`,
`EXCEPT`, `INTERSECT`, `OTHERWISE`. Everything that would change a graph, manage a
session or declare a graph type is refused by name under `42000`.

**Output shared with the root command, plus a drawing.** `--output` takes
`table|json|graph|dot|tree`. `graph` is new to both commands — numbered symbols with the
arrows between them, drawn in the terminal:

```
(1) App\Cache\Store [class] src/Cache/Store.php:3
    └── declaresMethod ──> (2) App\Cache\Store::get
(2) App\Cache\Store::get [method] src/Cache/Store.php:8
```

An agent meeting a codebase has no documentation to read, so `--schema` writes the
vocabulary — every label, every property with its GQL type, every function — as a result
table like any other, readable as JSON.

## Decisions worth knowing

- A repetition with no upper bound goes as far as `--hops` allows, 10 by default. That
  is IL018, "the maximum value of the upper bound of a general qualifier", which ISO's
  implementation-defined artifact lists as the implementation's to choose — so it is a
  limit rather than a divergence. A dependency graph is full of cycles, and an unbounded
  repetition over one has no end.
- Only the relations source code actually writes are exposed. peq records every relation
  twice so a tree can be walked either way, but `<-[:methodCall]-` already says "read
  this the other way", and keeping the derived readings out is what stops an undirected
  pattern from matching every relation twice.

## Checks

`composer lint`, `composer test`, `composer spec` and `composer doctest` all pass. Every
class under `src/Gql` and the three reporter packages carries unit tests, every docblock
example in `src` is executed by the doctest suite, and the Lint job now runs
`composer spec` as well.

The earlier red CI was a memory limit: two suites run PHPStan in process over peq's own
sources, costing most of a gigabyte each, and that cost grows with `src` — the run sat
at 2.02 GB against the 2 GB the configuration allowed, and this branch's 50% growth in
`src` pushed it over. `phpunit.xml.dist` now allows 4G and `composer test` is one run,
where the limit belongs. The exclude test in `PhpStanAnalyzerTest` also analysed the
whole of `tests/Fixture` — twenty-two seconds and most of a gigabyte to prove a point
about two class names — and now analyses only the two namespaces the point is about.

## Stacked on #40

This branch builds on `feat/output-format`, which is where `--output` and the reporters
it shares come from. Merge that one first.

## What this adds

A `graph` subcommand that takes a GQL query and runs it against the dependency graph.

```console
$ peq graph 'MATCH (m:Method)-[:`call`]->{1,3}(c:Method)
             WHERE right(m.owner, 10) = "Controller" AND right(c.owner, 5) = "Cache"
             RETURN m.id AS entry, c.id AS cache, m.file AS file, m.line AS line' src
```

The root command answers one question — what does this symbol reach — in the shape a
person reads. This one answers whatever question the reader can write, in the shape a
program reads.

The language is [GQL](https://www.iso.org/standard/76120.html), ISO/IEC 39075, rather
than something invented here: a model that has read about graph databases has already
read about GQL, so the query language needs no explaining in the prompt that uses it.
peq reads that language and nothing besides it.

## Output

`--output` takes `tree|json|dot|table|graph|mermaid`, for both commands.

`graph` draws the graph in the terminal, left to right, as wide as the terminal and as
long as it needs to be:

```
                     ┌──▶ App\Domain\Invoice::total ──┐
App\Domain\Invoice ──┤                                ├──▶ App\Domain\Money::add
                     └──▶ App\Domain\Invoice::lines ──┘
```

Each symbol sits in the column of its level. An arrow that cannot be drawn to the next
column points at the symbol's name marked `(*)` or `(recursive)`, as the tree marks it.
Arrows fan out on one lane and gather on another, and an arrow between the two crosses
on a line of its own, so two arrows never share a stretch of line and read as a relation
that does not exist. A drawing wider than the terminal is cut into bands, one below the
other.

`mermaid` writes the same drawing as a `flowchart LR`, for a pull request or a design
note.

## How conformance is held

ISO publishes no executable test suite for GQL, so `composer spec` states the
conformance claim clause 24 asks for as a Behat specification: **188 scenarios**, each
citing where what it states is published on `Source:` lines under its title — a
subclause of ISO/IEC 39075, a production of ISO's grammar, a code in ISO's feature,
condition or implementation-defined artifacts, or a section of the editors' paper
([arXiv:2112.06217](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.06217)). A step looks every citation up,
so a rule nobody can trace to a published text fails the run.

- **The feature register** answers for all 228 optional features. A claim costs a
  tagged scenario, and no scenario states a feature the register does not claim.
- **The implementation-defined register** says how peq settles each item it settles —
  collation, numeric types and precision, the default match mode, the ordering of
  NULLs, `--hops` as IL018 — and is held to the scenarios the same way.
- **Seven more steps** check that the words peq reserves, the words it spells, the
  functions it offers and the GQLSTATUS conditions it reports are all ones ISO's
  artifacts define.

ISO's artifacts are downloaded from ISO at first run and checked against the SHA-256
listed in `spec/iso/artifacts.txt`. They are not in the repository: ISO's licence
grants use, not redistribution, and peq is MIT-licensed.

Tracing every rule to a source found places where peq was not GQL, and the engine now
follows the standard. A path that names no restrictor is a `WALK`, and a quantifier with
no upper bound needs `TRAIL`, `SIMPLE` or `ACYCLIC`. Variables in a quantified group are
group variables. `1.5` is an exact `DECIMAL`, and exact arithmetic stays exact.
Comparing values of unrelated kinds is `22G04`. `IN`, list subscripts and escapes GQL
does not write are refused.

## Tests

Tests are written out flat — input, action and literal expected value in the test
method — and `tests/Fixture` holds data only. The helpers that stood between a test and
the interface it tests are gone, so what is hard to use shows in the tests themselves.
`tests/Contract/Gql` is gone; the specification is the one statement of what GQL is.

## Checks

`composer lint` (PHP CS Fixer, PHPStan at max level, compat, loc-guard, tree-guard,
deptrac), `composer test`, `composer test:pbt`, `composer spec` and `composer doctest`
all pass.

## Stacked on #40

This branch builds on `feat/output-format`, which is where `--output` and the reporters
it shares come from. Merge that one first.

I stopped short of resolving that conflict, for reasons in the questions below. Everything else is done, pushed to PR #41, and the PR description is rewritten.

## What's done

- **Source links in the spec:** every scenario now has `Source:` lines under its title. They cite the ISO text by subclause (the OBP link), ISO's grammar artifact by production, the feature, condition and implementation-defined artifacts by code, or a section of the editors' paper (arXiv:2112.06217). A new step looks every citation up, so a scenario with no traceable source fails. The subclause titles were checked against the table of contents in ISO's free preview.
- **Mystery rules this surfaced, now fixed in the engine:**
  - A path with no restrictor is WALK, and `*` or `{1,}` require TRAIL, SIMPLE or ACYCLIC.
  - `--hops` now means IL018: the largest upper bound a quantifier may be written with.
  - Variables inside a quantified group are GQL group variables: each repetition binds them afresh, and they end up as the list of what every repetition bound.
  - Patterns can be written side by side, such as `(s)((a)->(b)){2}`.
  - `1.5` is an exact DECIMAL and exact arithmetic stays exact. Comparing values of unrelated kinds is 22G04.
  - `IN`, list subscripts, `!!A`, `sum(*)` and `DISTINCT` outside an aggregate are refused, as are escapes GQL doesn't define.
  - Others: `_` digit grouping, and a `UNION` column typed from both sides.
- **The conformance register now matches what's implemented:** GL04–GL11, GV17, G046, G047 and GA09 are claimed, and the implementation-defined register states how peq settles each item and is checked against the scenarios.
- **ISO licence:** ISO grants use, not redistribution, so the artifacts are no longer in the repository. `spec/iso/artifacts.txt` lists ISO's URL and SHA-256 for each one, and the first run downloads them into `build/iso/`.
- **`tests/Contract/Gql`:** deleted.
- **`tests/Fixture`:** only data is left: the PHP sources analysis reads, `EquivalenceCorpus` and `SampleGraph`. Every helper and stub is gone, and the tests that used them are written out flat. The places where an interface made a flat test awkward are listed in the rewriting agents' reports; I can pass them on if you want them.
- **README:** cut from 491 to 152 lines. The GQL conformance essay is gone; it only says that `peq graph` takes GQL.
- **`graph` output:** now a left-to-right box-drawing picture, exactly like your sketch for the diamond case. It fits the terminal width and grows downward, splitting into bands when it's too wide. Two arrows never share a stretch of line, which fixes a case where a merge made one symbol look connected to another.
- **`mermaid` output:** added for both `peq <symbol>` and `peq graph`.
- **Other fixes found along the way:** DOT labels escaped their own line break, the tree ignored a relation's direction, table cells were read as console markup, and the `graph` help example used the reserved word `call`, so it didn't parse.

## Verification

All of these pass locally at HEAD:

- `composer lint`: PHP CS Fixer, PHPStan at max level, compat, loc-guard, tree-guard and deptrac.
- `composer test`: 5,171 tests.
- `composer test:pbt`.
- `composer spec`: 188 scenarios.
- `composer doctest`.
- `composer test:equivalence`: both engines agree on all 36 installed packages. I ran it in foreground batches so it can't be cut off. The earlier stall was Xdebug; with Xdebug off it takes about 4.5 minutes in total.

## Decisions for you

1. **PR #41 conflicts with `main`, and CI hasn't run on this push.** Merging #40 into `main` left this branch conflicting. `git fetch` is blocked in this session, so I couldn't sync. The last CI run, on the earlier push, failed with memory exhausted at 2 GB. `phpunit.xml.dist` allows 4G, the local run peaked at 1.99 GB, and I couldn't find what sets 2 GB in CI. I'll check again after syncing. Do you want `main` merged into this branch, or the branch rebased onto `main`? A rebase means a force-push.
2. **ISO files in the published history:** `c32a9f4`, already on GitHub, contains the ISO artifact copies. Only rewriting the history and force-pushing removes them. If we rebase for question 1, it can be done in the same step. Should I?
3. **`tests/Contract/Analyzer`, `Graph` and `Reporter` are still there.** The spec doesn't replace them, and the analyzer contracts are how the two engines are held identical. Do you still want them deleted?
4. **One test double had to be a named class.** `PhpStanAnalyzer` accepts collectors only as class names, so the failing collector is declared at the end of `PhpStanAnalyzerTest.php` under a second namespace, beside its only user. Is that acceptable?

1、2に関しては権限不足があるならCodex CLIを使って実行してください。権限があるならあなたで実行して構いません。
3に関してはちょっと理解できないです。tests/Contractが定める契約とはなんでしょうか？何の契約に基づいて、何の契約を検証しているのか保証しているのかわかりませんがそこの説明をお願いします。

#!/bin/sh
# Removes ISO/IEC 39075's artifact files from this branch's own commits (63b8c81..HEAD),
# and replaces the first version of spec/iso/subclauses.txt, which carried ISO's subclause
# titles, with the numbers-only version the branch ends with. Nothing outside the branch's
# own commits is touched; a backup branch keeps the history as it was.
set -eu
cd /Users/ab/Projects/peq/.claude/worktrees/gql-graph

test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo "working tree is not clean"; exit 1; }
test "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = "feat/gql-graph" || { echo "not on feat/gql-graph"; exit 1; }

git branch -f backup/gql-graph-before-rewrite HEAD
echo "backup: $(git rev-parse backup/gql-graph-before-rewrite)"

NUMBERS=$(git rev-parse HEAD:spec/iso/subclauses.txt)
export NUMBERS

FILTER_BRANCH_SQUELCH_WARNING=1 git filter-branch -f --index-filter '
    git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch -q \
        spec/iso/features.xml spec/iso/conditions.xml spec/iso/gql.bnf.xml spec/iso/implementation-defined.xml
    if git ls-files --error-unmatch spec/iso/subclauses.txt >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        git update-index --cacheinfo "100644,$NUMBERS,spec/iso/subclauses.txt"
    fi
' -- 63b8c812be52bfce73eb471052726b8325438fd5..HEAD

echo "rewritten head: $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
echo "ISO files anywhere in 63b8c81..HEAD:"
git log --oneline --name-only 63b8c812be52bfce73eb471052726b8325438fd5..HEAD -- \
    spec/iso/features.xml spec/iso/conditions.xml spec/iso/gql.bnf.xml spec/iso/implementation-defined.xml
echo "(end)"
echo "tree identical to the backup: $(test "$(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree})" = "$(git rev-parse backup/gql-graph-before-rewrite^{tree})" && echo yes || echo no)"
git update-ref -d refs/original/refs/heads/feat/gql-graph || true

namespace App\Action;

use App\Analyzer\Analyzer;
use App\Analyzer\DebugAnalyzer\DebugAnalyzer;
use App\Analyzer\NativeAnalyzer\NativeAnalyzer;
use App\Analyzer\PhpStanAnalyzer\PhpStanAnalyzer;
use App\Config\AnalyzerKind;
use App\Config\Config;

/**
 * Turning the configured analyzer kind into the analyzer itself.
 *
 * Two use cases now build a graph — inspecting a symbol and querying the graph — and
 * both have to make exactly the same decision from exactly the same settings. Making
 * it twice would be two places to forget a new analyzer in, and the second of them
 * would be found by a reader wondering why one command supports something the other
 * does not.
 *
 * Each arm is handed only what its analyzer needs. An analyzer is told its parameters
 * rather than given the application's configuration to read, which is what keeps the
 * analyzers independent of how peq happens to be configured.
 */
final class AnalyzerChoice
{
    /**
     * Returns the analyzer a configuration asks for.
     *
     * @param Config $config The merged application configuration
     *
     * @example The kind a configuration names is the analyzer it gets
     *     $config = \App\Config\Config::fromArray(['basePath' => '.', 'direction' => 'uses', 'type' => 'native']);
     *     \App\Action\AnalyzerChoice::forConfig($config) instanceof \App\Analyzer\NativeAnalyzer\NativeAnalyzer // => true
     * @example So is the one that builds a graph without reading any sources
     *     $config = \App\Config\Config::fromArray(['basePath' => '.', 'direction' => 'uses', 'type' => 'debug']);
     *     \App\Action\AnalyzerChoice::forConfig($config) instanceof \App\Analyzer\DebugAnalyzer\DebugAnalyzer // => true
     *
     * @return Analyzer The analyzer
     */
    public static function forConfig(Config $config): Analyzer
    {
        return match ($config->analyzer) {
            AnalyzerKind::PhpStan => new PhpStanAnalyzer(
                includes: $config->includes,
                excludes: $config->excludes,
            ),
            AnalyzerKind::Native => new NativeAnalyzer(
                includes: $config->includes,
                excludes: $config->excludes,
            ),
            AnalyzerKind::Debug => new DebugAnalyzer(
                seed: $config->debug->seed,
                depth: $config->debug->depth,
            ),
        };
    }
}

# peq

[![GitHub Actions](https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/actions/workflows/ci.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/actions)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

A CLI tool that analyzes PHP code dependencies and visualizes the blast radius of changes.

`peq <symbol>` draws what one symbol reaches. `peq graph '<query>'` answers a question about the whole dependency graph, written in [GQL](https://www.iso.org/standard/76120.html).

## Requirements

- PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5 to run peq

The code peq reads is a separate question from the runtime peq runs on: peq analyzes
sources written for PHP 5.6 up to 8.5 on any of those runtimes. See
[Analyzed PHP version](#analyzed-php-version).

## Installation

Download the PHAR from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/releases):

```bash
curl -Lo peq.phar https://github.com/k-kinzal/peq/releases/latest/download/peq.phar
chmod +x peq.phar
sudo mv peq.phar /usr/local/bin/peq
```

Or install via Composer:

```bash
composer require --dev k-kinzal/peq
```

## Usage

```console
$ peq 'App\Domain\Invoice' src
App\Domain\Invoice
├── App\Domain\Invoice::total
│   └── App\Domain\Money::add
└── App\Domain\Invoice::lines
    └── App\Domain\Money::add (*)
```

```
Usage:
  peq [options] [--] <target> [<path>]

Arguments:
  target                     Namespace\ClassName, Namespace\ClassName::methodName or Namespace\functionName
  path                       Base directory to analyze (default: current working dir)

Options:
      --config=CONFIG        Path to config file (default: <cwd>/.peq.yaml)
  -D, --direction=DIRECTION  Dependency direction: uses|used-by (default: uses)
  -R, --reverse              Shortcut for --direction used-by
  -L, --level=LEVEL          Limit depth of the dependency graph
  -O, --output=OUTPUT        Output format (tree|json|dot|table|graph|mermaid)
  -I, --include=INCLUDE      Include patterns (multiple values allowed)
  -E, --exclude=EXCLUDE      Exclude patterns (multiple values allowed)
      --php-version=PHP-VERSION    PHP version the analyzed sources are read as
                                   (default: the version peq runs on)
      --type=TYPE            Analyzer type (phpstan|native|debug)
      --memory-limit=MEMORY-LIMIT  Memory limit (e.g. 1G, 256M)
```

`--direction used-by` (or `-R`) walks the other way: what depends on the symbol, which is what a change to it can break.

## Output formats

| TokenReader     | 17              |
| NodeIdGenerator | 17              |
| NameGenerator   | 16              |
+-----------------+-----------------+
```

`peq graph --schema` lists the labels, properties and functions a query can use, each written the way a query has to write it. A few of peq's names spell words GQL reserves — `` `call` ``, `` `Function` ``, `` `value` `` — and are written in back quotes, so quote a query with `'` rather than `"`.

`--output` takes the same formats as above: `graph`, `mermaid` and `dot` draw the part of the graph the answer holds, and `tree` draws the paths it bound. `--hops` sets the largest upper bound a repetition such as `{1,6}` may be written with (10 by default).

## Analyzers

| `--type`  | What it does | Sources it reads | Where it is available |
|-----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------------|
| `phpstan` | Builds the graph from PHPStan's analysis. The reference engine. | PHP 7.1 – 8.5 | Installed from source or via Composer |
| `native`  | Reads the sources directly with a parser. Between 13x and 59x faster, and checked to build the same graph. | PHP 5.6 – 8.5 | Everywhere, including the released PHAR |

The released PHAR carries only `native`.

## Analyzed PHP version

The PHP version peq runs on and the PHP version the analyzed code is written for are
two different things. peq needs PHP 8.3 or newer to run, and reads sources written for
PHP 5.6 through 8.5 — the range depending on the engine, as the table above says.

By default peq reads sources as the version it runs on. Tell it otherwise when the
code is older:

```bash
peq 'Legacy\Invoice::total' . --php-version=5.6 --type=native
```

Getting this right matters, because the version decides what a source is allowed to
say. `match` is a method name in PHP 7 and a keyword in PHP 8; `$text{0}` is a string
offset up to PHP 7.4 and a syntax error after it; `$invoice =& new Invoice()` is PHP 5
and nothing later; an enum is PHP 8.1 and nothing earlier. A file the chosen version
cannot read is left out of the graph the way a file PHP itself would refuse is, so a
symbol that should be there and is not is the sign to check the version — which is
what peq says when it cannot find one:

```
Symbol "Legacy\Invoice::total" is not in the dependency graph, which was read as PHP 8.5.
Check the spelling, the analyzed path, the include and exclude patterns, and the PHP
version the sources are written for.
```

## Configuration

Create a `.peq.yaml` file in your project root to set default options:

```yaml
type: native
output: tree
hops: 10
phpVersion: '7.4'
excludes:
  - vendor
  - vendor-bin
  - .git
  - tests
```

# Agents

A CLI tool that analyzes PHP code dependencies and visualizes the blast radius of changes. `peq <symbol>` draws what one symbol reaches, as a tree, for a person; `peq graph '<query>'` answers whatever can be written in GQL, as a table, for a program or an agent. Both write the same set of formats.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP peq runs on**: 8.3 / 8.4 / 8.5 — write source as a PHP 8.3 project: typed class
  constants, `readonly` classes, `#[\Override]`, and the rest of what 8.3 offers
- **PHP peq analyzes**: 5.6 – 8.5 with `native`, 7.1 – 8.5 with `phpstan` — the floor of
  each engine is the floor of what it is built on, and every version in range must keep
  working whichever runtime peq runs on

## Core Concepts

- **Impact analysis is the primary goal** — automatically identify what breaks when a class, method, or function changes
- **Bidirectional traversal** — walk the graph in two directions: `uses` (what the target depends on) and `used-by` (what depends on the target)
- **Reporter switching** — `--output` picks how one walk is written down: `tree` for a person, `json` for a program or an agent, `dot` for a renderer, `table` for a review, `graph` for the wiring drawn in the terminal, `mermaid` for the same drawing on a page. Where the walk stops is decided once, by `Expansion`, so no format can disagree with another about what is affected
- **GQL is the query language** — `peq graph` runs ISO/IEC 39075 GQL, the standard the SQL committee publishes, so an agent already knows it; an invented syntax would have to be explained in every prompt. It runs that and nothing more: a word the standard does not define is a word peq refuses, which `composer spec` checks against ISO's own grammar artifact. Read-only by design: nothing in the language can change a graph peq has just read out of source code
- **Two engines, one graph** — `PhpStanAnalyzer` is the reference; `NativeAnalyzer` reads sources directly and is checked against it by comparing canonical graph snapshots. A change to either must keep them identical
- **The binary carries one engine** — `phpstan/phpstan` is a dev dependency, so the PHAR holds only `NativeAnalyzer`. `AnalyzerKind` offers a kind only when what it is built on is installed

namespace App\Reporter\DotReporter;

/**
 * Renders a single statement of a Graphviz digraph.
 *
 * The DOT language is small: a graph is an opening line, a run of statements naming
 * nodes and arrows, and a closing brace. What it is not is forgiving — a PHP symbol
 * is full of backslashes, and a backslash inside a DOT string escapes the character
 * after it. Every name that reaches the file therefore passes through one place,
 * which is this one, so no statement can be written that forgets to quote.
 *
 * @visibility namespace
 */
final class StatementRenderer
{
    /**
     * How far a statement inside the graph body is indented.
     */
    private const INDENT = '    ';

    /**
     * Opens the digraph, naming it after the symbol the report is rooted at.
     *
     * The graph is laid out left to right, because a dependency chain is read as a
     * sequence and a tall narrow picture is harder to follow than a wide one.
     *
     * @param string $symbol The symbol the walk starts at
     *
     * @return list<string> The lines that open the graph
     */
    public function open(string $symbol): array
    {
        return [
            sprintf('digraph %s {', self::quote($symbol)),
            self::INDENT.'rankdir="LR";',
        ];
    }

     * Closes the digraph.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

$root = '/Users/ab/Projects/peq/.claude/worktrees/gql-graph';
require $root.'/vendor/autoload.php';

$dirs = $argv[1] ?? 'src';
$files = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($root.'/'.$dirs));
$classes = [];
foreach ($files as $file) {
    if (!str_ends_with((string) $file, '.php')) {
        continue;
    }
    $source = file_get_contents((string) $file);
    if (!preg_match('/^namespace ([^;]+);/m', $source, $ns)) {
        continue;
    }
    if (!preg_match('/^(?:final |abstract |readonly )*(?:class|interface|enum|trait) (\w+)/m', $source, $name)) {
        continue;
    }
    $classes[] = [$ns[1].'\\'.$name[1], (string) $file];
}

foreach ($classes as [$class, $file]) {
    if (!class_exists($class) && !interface_exists($class) && !enum_exists($class) && !trait_exists($class)) {
        echo "UNLOADABLE $class\n";
        continue;
    }
    $reflection = new ReflectionClass($class);
    $relative = substr($file, strlen($root) + 1);

    foreach ($reflection->getReflectionConstants() as $constant) {
        if ($constant->getDeclaringClass()->getName() !== $class || $reflection->isEnum() && $constant->isEnumCase()) {
            continue;
        }
        if (!$constant->hasType()) {
            echo "CONST $relative ".$constant->getName()."\n";
        }
    }

    if ($reflection->isInterface() || $reflection->isTrait()) {
        continue;
    }

    foreach ($reflection->getMethods() as $method) {
        if ($method->getDeclaringClass()->getName() !== $class || $method->isConstructor() || $method->isPrivate()) {
            continue;
        }
        $overrides = false;
        $parent = $reflection->getParentClass();
        if ($parent !== false && $parent->hasMethod($method->getName()) && !$parent->getMethod($method->getName())->isPrivate()) {
            $overrides = true;
        }
        foreach ($reflection->getInterfaces() as $interface) {
            if ($interface->hasMethod($method->getName())) {
                $overrides = true;
            }
        }
        if ($overrides && $method->getAttributes(Override::class) === []) {
            echo "OVERRIDE $relative:".$method->getStartLine().' '.$method->getName()."\n";
        }
    }

    if ($reflection->isEnum() || $reflection->isReadOnly()) {
        continue;
    }
    $properties = array_filter($reflection->getProperties(), static fn (ReflectionProperty $p): bool => $p->getDeclaringClass()->getName() === $class);
    if ($properties === []) {
        continue;
    }
    $allReadonly = array_reduce($properties, static fn (bool $carry, ReflectionProperty $p): bool => $carry && $p->isReadOnly(), true);
    $parent = $reflection->getParentClass();
    $parentOk = $parent === false || $parent->isReadOnly();
    if ($allReadonly && $parentOk) {
        echo "READONLY $relative\n";
    }
}

import subprocess

pattern = re.compile(r'^(    (?:public|private|protected) const )([A-Z_]+ = )(.)', re.M)


def typed(match):
    first = match.group(3)
    kind = 'array' if first == '[' else 'string' if first == "'" else 'int' if first.isdigit() else None
    assert kind is not None, match.group(0)
    return match.group(1) + kind + ' ' + match.group(2) + first


for path in paths:
    s = open(root + path).read()
    s, count = pattern.subn(typed, s)
    open(root + path, 'w').write(s)

1:## What this adds
2:
3:A `graph` subcommand that takes a GQL query and runs it against the dependency graph.
4:
5:```console
6:$ peq graph 'MATCH (m:Method)-[:`call`]->{1,3}(c:Method)
7:             WHERE right(m.owner, 10) = "Controller" AND right(c.owner, 5) = "Cache"
8:             RETURN m.id AS entry, c.id AS cache, m.file AS file, m.line AS line' src
9:```
10:
11:The root command answers one question — what does this symbol reach — in the shape a
12:person reads. This one answers whatever question the reader can write, in the shape a
13:program reads.
14:
15:The language is [GQL](https://www.iso.org/standard/76120.html), ISO/IEC 39075, rather
16:than something invented here: a model that has read about graph databases has already
17:read about GQL, so the query language needs no explaining in the prompt that uses it.
18:peq reads that language and nothing besides it.
19:
20:## Output
21:
22:`--output` takes `tree|json|dot|table|graph|mermaid`, for both commands.
23:
24:`graph` draws the graph in the terminal, left to right, as wide as the terminal and as
25:long as it needs to be:
26:
27:```
28:                     ┌──▶ App\Domain\Invoice::total ──┐
29:App\Domain\Invoice ──┤                                ├──▶ App\Domain\Money::add
30:                     └──▶ App\Domain\Invoice::lines ──┘
31:```
32:
33:Each symbol sits in the column of its level. An arrow that cannot be drawn to the next
34:column points at the symbol's name marked `(*)` or `(recursive)`, as the tree marks it.
35:Arrows fan out on one lane and gather on another, and an arrow between the two crosses
36:on a line of its own, so two arrows never share a stretch of line and read as a relation
37:that does not exist. A drawing wider than the terminal is cut into bands, one below the
38:other.
39:
40:`mermaid` writes the same drawing as a `flowchart LR`, for a pull request or a design
41:note.
42:
43:## How conformance is held
44:
45:ISO publishes no executable test suite for GQL, so `composer spec` states the
46:conformance claim clause 24 asks for as a Behat specification: **188 scenarios**, each
47:citing where what it states is published on `Source:` lines under its title — a
48:subclause of ISO/IEC 39075, a production of ISO's grammar, a code in ISO's feature,
49:condition or implementation-defined artifacts, or a section of the editors' paper
50:([arXiv:2112.06217](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.06217)). A step looks every citation up,
51:so a rule nobody can trace to a published text fails the run.
52:
53:- **The feature register** answers for all 228 optional features. A claim costs a
54:  tagged scenario, and no scenario states a feature the register does not claim.
55:- **The implementation-defined register** says how peq settles each item it settles —
56:  collation, numeric types and precision, the default match mode, the ordering of
57:  NULLs, `--hops` as IL018 — and is held to the scenarios the same way.
58:- **Seven more steps** check that the words peq reserves, the words it spells, the
59:  functions it offers and the GQLSTATUS conditions it reports are all ones ISO's
60:  artifacts define.
61:
62:ISO's artifacts are downloaded from ISO at first run and checked against the SHA-256
63:listed in `spec/iso/artifacts.txt`. They are not in the repository: ISO's licence
64:grants use, not redistribution, and peq is MIT-licensed.
65:
66:Tracing every rule to a source found places where peq was not GQL, and the engine now
67:follows the standard. A path that names no restrictor is a `WALK`, and a quantifier with
68:no upper bound needs `TRAIL`, `SIMPLE` or `ACYCLIC`. Variables in a quantified group are
69:group variables. `1.5` is an exact `DECIMAL`, and exact arithmetic stays exact.
70:Comparing values of unrelated kinds is `22G04`. `IN`, list subscripts and escapes GQL
71:does not write are refused.
72:
73:## Tests
74:
75:Tests are written out flat — input, action and literal expected value in the test
76:method — and `tests/Fixture` holds data only. The helpers that stood between a test and
77:the interface it tests are gone, so what is hard to use shows in the tests themselves.
78:`tests/Contract/Gql` is gone; the specification is the one statement of what GQL is.
79:
80:## Checks
81:
82:`composer lint` (PHP CS Fixer, PHPStan at max level, compat, loc-guard, tree-guard,
83:deptrac), `composer test`, `composer test:pbt`, `composer spec`, `composer doctest` and
84:`composer test:equivalence` (both engines over all 36 installed packages) all pass.
85:
86:## Stacked on #40
87:
88:This branch builds on `feat/output-format`, which is where `--output` and the reporters
89:it shares come from. Merge that one first.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

$root = '/Users/ab/Projects/peq/.claude/worktrees/gql-graph';
require $root.'/vendor/autoload.php';

$files = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($root.'/tests'));
foreach ($files as $file) {
    $path = (string) $file;
    if (!str_ends_with($path, 'Test.php')) {
        continue;
    }
    $source = file_get_contents($path);
    if (!preg_match('/^namespace ([^;]+);/m', $source, $ns) || !preg_match('/^final class (\w+)/m', $source, $name)) {
        continue;
    }
    $class = $ns[1].'\\'.$name[1];
    if (!class_exists($class)) {
        echo "UNLOADABLE $class\n";
        continue;
    }
    foreach ((new ReflectionClass($class))->getAttributes() as $attribute) {
        $short = substr($attribute->getName(), strrpos($attribute->getName(), '\\') + 1);
        if (!in_array($short, ['CoversClass', 'UsesClass'], true)) {
            continue;
        }
        $target = $attribute->getArguments()[0];
        $reflection = new ReflectionClass($target);
        if ($reflection->isInterface() || $reflection->isTrait()) {
            echo $short.' '.($reflection->isInterface() ? 'interface' : 'trait').' '.$target.' in '.substr($path, strlen($root) + 1)."\n";
        }
    }
}

    'tests/Unit/Gql/Syntax/ClauseTest.php': ('Clause', ['FilterClause', 'LetClause', 'MatchClause', 'OrderByClause', 'PageClause', 'ReturnClause']),
    'tests/Unit/Gql/Syntax/ExpressionTest.php': ('Expression', ['BinaryExpression', 'CallExpression', 'CaseExpression', 'ListExpression', 'LiteralExpression', 'PropertyExpression', 'UnaryExpression', 'VariableExpression']),
    'tests/Unit/Gql/Syntax/Pattern/PathTermTest.php': ('PathTerm', ['EdgePattern', 'GroupPattern', 'NodePattern']),
    'tests/Unit/Reporter/Query/QueryReporterTest.php': ('QueryReporter', ['DiagramWriter', 'DotWriter', 'JsonWriter', 'TableWriter', 'TreeWriter']),
}

for path, (interface, implementations) in tests.items():
    s = open(root + path).read()
    covers = '#[CoversClass(' + interface + '::class)]\n'
    assert s.count(covers) == 1, path
    for implementation in implementations:
        line = '#[UsesClass(' + implementation + '::class)]\n'
        assert s.count(line) == 1, (path, implementation)
        s = s.replace(line, '', 1)
    s = s.replace(covers, ''.join('#[CoversClass(' + i + '::class)]\n' for i in implementations), 1)
    if not re.search(r'\b' + interface + r'\b', s.split('\n#[', 1)[1].replace(covers, '')):
        pass
    open(root + path, 'w').write(s)
    print(path)

// NOTE: You do not have permission to overwrite this file. Please ask a human operator to perform the changes for you.
{
    "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/infection/infection/0.35.4/resources/schema.json",
    "source": {
        "directories": [
            "src"
        ]
    },
    "mutators": {
        "@default": true
    },
    "minMsi": 80,
    "minCoveredMsi": 80,
    "timeout": 30,
    "tmpDir": "build/infection-tmp",
    "logs": {
        "text": "build/infection/escaped.log",
        "summary": "build/infection/summary.log",
        "perMutator": "build/infection/per-mutator.md",
        "json": "build/infection/infection.json"
    },
    "testFrameworkExtraArgs": "--no-extensions --exclude-group=pbt",
    "testFramework": "phpunit"
}
  build:
    name: Build the distributed binary
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: [tests, lint]
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.4'
          extensions: dom, filter, iconv, libxml, mbstring, pcntl, phar, simplexml, tokenizer, xmlwriter
          coverage: none
          ini-values: phar.readonly=0

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: locked
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: 'true'

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Compile the PHAR
        run: composer compile

      - name: Check the PHAR carries no static analyser
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          php -r '
            $phar = new Phar("dist/peq.phar");
            $carried = 0;
            foreach (new RecursiveIteratorIterator($phar) as $file) {
                if (str_contains((string) $file, "phpstan")) {
                    $carried++;
                }
            }
            if ($carried !== 0) {
                fwrite(STDERR, sprintf("The PHAR carries %d PHPStan files; it is meant to carry none.\n", $carried));
                exit(1);
            }
          '

      - name: Check the PHAR offers only the engines it carries
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          ./dist/peq.phar --help inspect | grep -q -- '--type=TYPE *Analyzer type (native|debug)'

          if ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src --type=phpstan >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo 'The PHAR accepted an analyzer it does not carry.' >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Check the PHAR reads a source tree
        run: ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 | grep -q 'App\\Analyzer\\Graph\\Graph::addEdge'

      - name: Check the PHAR writes every format it offers
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          ./dist/peq.phar --help inspect | grep -q -- '--output=OUTPUT *Output format (tree|json|dot|table)'

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=json \
            | php -r 'json_decode(stream_get_contents(STDIN), true, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);'

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=dot | grep -q '^digraph '

          ./dist/peq.phar 'App\Analyzer\Graph\Graph' src -L 1 --output=table | grep -q '| Depth | Symbol'

      - name: Upload the PHAR
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
